# Copilot Instructions

## Project Guidelines
- When adding diagnostics to UE SDK wrapper functions in this project, use SPDLOG_INFO/WARN/ERROR macros (spdlog) consistent with existing files like AHUD.cpp, and log relevant pointers (e.g., uclass, this, result) to help pinpoint failure branches.
- In WuWa/UEVR Lua scripting, dynamically locate the active instance of LGUI's LGUIEventSystem by finding the one with a non-nil selection, rather than assuming a singleton. Use its InputTrigger/InputNavigationUp/InputNavigationDown methods for native gamepad confirm/back/navigation instead of emulating mouse/cursor input.
- In the UEVR codebase, ensure that watchdog/backoff timers that gate on a flickering/noisy stalled-state signal (e.g. VR::is_engine_tick_stalled) reset ALL related timestamps used in the outer trigger condition, not just a subset, to prevent the backoff from being defeated on the next poll when the signal transiently flips.
- In the UEVR codebase, when accessing native resources or calling methods that can potentially fail (like get_native_resource(), GetDesc(), etc.), always check for nullptr before dereferencing. Use defensive null checks before all pointer dereferences, wrap risky operations in null checks, and provide fallback code paths. Log warnings via SPDLOG_WARN when fallbacks are triggered to aid diagnostics.
- In the UEVR codebase, methods that return object managers or renderers (like get_render_target_manager()) can return nullptr, especially during state transitions or menu changes. Always capture the return value in a temporary variable and check for nullptr BEFORE chaining method calls. Never do method_chain()->other_method() without checking each level for nullptr first, as this causes silent null pointer dereferences during transitions.
- When a diagnostic/A-B-test hypothesis in the UEVR NSF stereo rendering hook is disproven by in-headset testing (e.g. blocking a view causes it to stick to the HMD or introduces a constant offset), fully revert the associated guard logic, toggles, and UI in FFakeStereoRenderingHook.cpp, VR.hpp, and VR.cpp back to unconditional/original behavior rather than leaving partial gating in place.
- In the UEVR codebase's exception-handler UAF recovery (FFakeStereoRenderingHook.cpp), do not redirect recovered/faulting pointers to a valid dummy memory buffer as a 'safer than null' mitigation. Prefer the simpler fail-fast approach: force the destination register to a literal 0 so any follow-on bad dereference is caught immediately by the same handler, rather than allowing corrupted game logic to run further into a broken call chain before eventually crashing elsewhere.
- For LGUI view-extension hooks, prefer runtime discovery and validation of the correct candidate over hard-coded game-build-specific vtable RVAs.
- In the UEVR Wuthering Waves stereo/shadow fix work, diagnostic/experimental ModToggle options that turn out to be confirmed fixes (e.g. m_native_stereo_fix_mirror_fov) must be added to the main toggle serialization/config list (the array in VR.hpp used for saving/loading) so they persist across restarts, and their UI label/tooltip and doc comments should be updated to drop the 'DIAG'/'EXPERIMENTAL' framing once confirmed.
- In the UEVR Wuthering Waves NSF/right-eye-shadow-fix investigation, note that the CSM (Cascaded Shadow Maps) Transition Scale cvar, when set to 1, turns on environmental/cascade shadows only in the left eye (right eye still missing them); when set to 0, it turns shadows off for both eyes. This is a confirmed behavioral data point for diagnosing the right-eye cascade shadow fix.
- When adding diagnostics that perform GPU pixel sampling/readback in D3D12Component.cpp, reuse the existing diag_sample_texture() helper, gate the logging behind vr->is_diag_verbose_logging_enabled(), and throttle sample frequency (e.g. first N samples then every Mth) to avoid per-frame GPU stalls from the synchronous fence wait.

## Recovery Guidelines
- When Visual Studio crashes or unsaved edits are lost in this workspace, check .vs\CopilotSnapshots\ for recoverable file snapshots before assuming work is lost, and verify recovered content via diff against the current file before restoring.
